name: gh-issue
description: GitHub issue and discussion lifecycle: read, create, implement, directive-protocol execution, Discussion authoring and promotion.
skillInstructions:
Kimi Code tool mapping for the gh-issue skills.

The authoritative mapping is not in this repo. It lives in the sibling repo `dEitY719/harness-skills` at `references/kimi-tools.md` (https://github.com/dEitY719/harness-skills/blob/main/references/kimi-tools.md) and is the single source of truth for every repo in the `dEitY719/*-skills` family; do not copy it here. Summary:

- Read / Write / Edit / Bash / Grep / Glob keep their exposed Kimi names. Search contents with `Grep`; match paths with `Glob`. Every skill here drives the `gh` CLI -- run it with `Bash` and pass its output through verbatim.
- "Ask the user" -> `AskUserQuestion`. `gh-issue:create` uses it for its clarification guard, and `gh-issue:discussion-create` for category selection. A silent default is not the user's answer.
- `TodoWrite` -> Kimi Code's `TodoList` tool. `gh-issue:proceed` tracks its 8 protocol sections there.
- "Dispatch a subagent" -> `Agent` with `subagent_type: "coder"` (implementation) or `"explore"` (read-only). Never pass `general-purpose`.
- Claude Code's `Skill` tool has no Kimi equivalent. `gh-issue:implement` calls `superpowers:test-driven-development` on its TDD path; without a skill-invocation tool, take its built-in fallback path instead -- it is a complete flow, not a degraded one.
- All six need an authenticated `gh` CLI and carry `GH_HOST` plus `--repo` on every call, because `--repo` alone names no server.

Safety contracts. These are part of the skills, not advice:

- `gh-issue:read` never mutates. It prints the issue verbatim -- no summarising away the body, no reformatting comments.
- `gh-issue:create` never invents requirements the chat did not decide. A pre-decision RFC goes to `gh-issue:discussion-create` instead.
- `gh-issue:implement` never commits, never opens a PR, never runs on the default branch, never creates a worktree, and never fixes a test that was already failing before it edited anything. Its fallback path retries at most 3 times.
- `gh-issue:proceed` validates the protocol schema strictly and refuses to guess a missing section. Every write step passes its safety gate first.
- `gh-issue:discussion-convert` is idempotent: a Discussion already converted is recognised and not duplicated.
- A block label (`do-not-work`, `on-hold`, and the rest of `GH_ISSUE_BLOCK_LABELS`) is a hard refusal in both `implement` and `proceed`. There is no override flag -- removing the label is the only release.

interface.longDescription: gh-issue bundles the six issue/discussion lifecycle skills: read, create, implement, proceed, discussion-create, and discussion-convert.
